correctness.rationale: Writing each abundance as one plus an excess count reduces Berger–Parker ordering to the largest excess part and Simpson ordering to an excess quadratic sum. Exact extremal bounds prove no reversal through seven excess individuals, while exhaustive partition enumeration proves that eight is sharp and classifies the entire first layer. The finite-sample Simpson numerator differs from the population-form quadratic numerator by a fixed additive term at common total abundance.

value.rationale: Berger–Parker and Simpson are standard dominance summaries that deliberately weight the abundance profile differently. The smallest positive-integer resolution at which those weighting choices can reverse a community ranking is a natural structural benchmark. Expressing the result as an excess count makes the threshold independent of richness, and the complete first layer provides a reproducible diagnostic classification.
